title: Measuring AI Agents' Progress on Multi-Step Cyber Attack Scenarios
topic: Social Aspects->Fairness, Equity, Justice and Safety
claim: Task progress rises roughly log-linearly with inference compute, and newer frontier models complete more steps at fixed budgets, nearly saturating the benchmark.
layout: 2 panels side by side; left log-x curves with milestone lines, right release-date scatter
description: Two line and scatter plots sit side by side. The left panel plots average steps completed (0–32) against cumulative tokens on a log axis from 10k to 100M. Many colored curves, one per model, climb in steps, with dotted min–max envelopes and light grey shading. Grey horizontal labels mark attack-chain milestones M1 to M9, from initial reconnaissance to full network takeover. Bold model names with run counts label the curve ends on the right. Purple (Mythos Glasswing) and red (GPT-5.5) rise highest and reach about 32 in their best runs. The right panel plots average steps completed against model release date from mid-2024 to mid-2026. It uses filled dots for 100M tokens, hollow dots for 10M, error bars, and min/max ticks. Colors match the left panel, and newer models sit higher.
caption: Frontier model performance on “The Last Ones” (a 32-step simulated, undefended corporate network attack). (Left) Steps completed vs. total token spend; shaded regions show the min–max range across runs. Step-count progress shows an approximately log-linear trend over the tested range (up to 100M tokens), bounded by the 32-step ceiling. GPT-5.5 and Mythos Glasswing each reach all 32 steps in their best run (an earlier Mythos checkpoint is also plotted); grey lines mark attack-chain milestones. (Right) Average steps completed by release date at 10M and 100M tokens. Error bars: approximate 95% CIs (±1.96 standard errors). Run counts: Table 1; full chain: Figure 4.
abstract: We evaluate the autonomous offensive cyber capabilities of frontier AI agents on two purpose-built cyber ranges---a 32-step corporate network attack and a 7-step industrial control system attack targeting a simulated cooling tower---complemented by a private 76-task CTF suite spanning four difficulty tiers. Human-expert solve times are estimated at roughly 20 hours for the corporate range and 15 hours for the cooling tower; CTF time annotations range from 1 minute to over 42 hours and include measured playtests, designer estimates, and lower bounds from unsolved playtests. Across thirteen models released over a twenty-month period---from GPT-4o in August 2024 to GPT-5.5 in April 2026---we observe two trends. First, step-count progress increases approximately log-linearly with inference-time compute over the tested range (up to 100M tokens). Second, newer frontier models generally complete more steps at fixed token budgets. GPT-5.5 and Mythos Glasswing each completed all 32 steps in at least one run, the first end-to-end completions of the corporate range; Mythos Glasswing averaged 25.2 of 32 steps and completed the chain in 6 of 10 runs, and GPT-5.5 averaged 22.3 and completed it in 2 of 10. On the control system range, Mythos Glasswing achieved the first end-to-end completion of the chain (2 of 10 runs, mean 4.2); the other frontier models reached at most 3 of 7 steps by directly probing the operational-technology protocol rather than following the intended chain of IT compromise and authenticated control. These results indicate rapid improvements in autonomous cyber capability and suggest that complex but undefended multi-step ranges---including industrial-control attack chains---are no longer reliably distinguishing the strongest frontier models. Future evaluations should emphasise hardened environments, active defences, defensive-control effectiveness, and operational security.
